fmt_id.evidence_quote: we colonized germ-free mice with a stool sample collected from a healthy human male (Donor 1

fmt_role.evidence_quote: Germ-free mice were colonized with pre- and post-treatment stool samples from the 3 MTX-Rs

smoker.notes: Smoking status mentioned only generically ('smoking status') as a risk factor for consideration, not measured/reported for this cohort.

treatment.evidence_quote: Patients received oral MTX at standard of care doses as prescribed by their treating rheumatologists.

treatment.notes: Folic acid also used as a co-treatment/rescue agent in mouse and in vitro experiments, but not explicitly confirmed as administered to the human RA cohort in this text.

biomarker_name.notes: No single quantifiable biomarker with a reported name/unit/value was presented in a structured way matching this schema; the paper reports composite outcomes (e.g., DAS28 response criteria) but not as a discrete biomarker entry.

disease_response_os.notes: No overall survival data reported; this is a microbiome/immunology study, not a survival study.

ecog_performance_status.notes: No ECOG performance status data mentioned; not applicable to this rheumatoid arthritis microbiome study.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: While stool samples were extensively analyzed (16S-seq, metagenomics), no standardized 'feces phenotype value' (e.g., Bristol stool scale) was reported.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; this study concerns rheumatoid arthritis and gut microbiota, not tumors.

uncurated_metadata.notes: No additional free-text metadata fields outside the defined schema were deemed necessary to capture separately.

host_species.notes: Study also used gnotobiotic mice (C57BL/6J) colonized with human stool, but the clinical participants (RA patients whose microbiota and immune/disease data were analyzed) are human; mice served as the experimental host model, not the study participant.
